import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős–Ulam problem

The Erdős–Ulam problem asks whether the Euclidean plane contains a dense set of points
whose pairwise Euclidean distances are all rational numbers. The question was asked by
Ulam in 1946. It is open. Tao and Shaffaf observed that the Bombieri–Lang conjecture
implies a negative answer, and Pasten showed that the abc conjecture also implies a
negative answer.

The same problem appears as Erdős Problem 212, formalized in
`FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«212»` with the plane modeled as `ℂ`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Ulam_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)
- [Sh18] Shaffaf, J., *A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming
  the Bombieri–Lang conjecture*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 60 (2018), 283–293.
  [arXiv:1501.00159](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00159)
- [SdZ10] Solymosi, J. and de Zeeuw, F., *On a question of Erdős and Ulam*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. 43 (2010), 393–401. [arXiv:0806.3095](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3095)
-/

namespace ErdosUlamProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
**Erdős–Ulam problem.** Is there a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is dense in the
Euclidean plane and such that the Euclidean distance between any two points of $S$ is a
rational number?

Here "dense" means topologically dense in the whole plane $\mathbb{R}^2$, and the distance
condition is required for every pair of points of $S$ (it holds trivially for a point and
itself, since the distance is $0$).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 52]
theorem erdos_ulam_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q) := by
  sorry

end ErdosUlamProblem
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement; the notes' reading (topological density in all of ℝ², Euclidean distance rational, p = q trivial, `answer(sorry)` for an open yes/no question) is the one implemented.
modeling_decisions: The plane is modeled as `ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (repo scoped notation from `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean`), so `dist` is the Euclidean (L2) distance, as in the sibling file `Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean`.

'Dense' is formalized as Mathlib's topological `Dense S` for `S : Set ℝ²`, i.e. dense in the whole plane (not merely infinite or dense on a curve). `Dense ∅` is false, so the empty set is not a degenerate witness.

'Rational distance' is formalized as `¬ Irrational (dist p q)`, which unfolds to `dist p q ∈ Set.range Rat.cast`; this matches the idiom in `Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean`. The condition is imposed on all pairs `p, q ∈ S` including `p = q`, where it holds trivially (distance 0), so this is equivalent to the `Set.Pairwise` form.

The question is stated with `answer(sorry)`: `answer(True)` is a positive answer (such a set exists), `answer(False)` the negative (conjectured) one. The problem is open, so `research open` is used and the conditional results (Bombieri–Lang / abc) are only mentioned in the module docstring.

The same problem is already formalized as Erdős Problem 212 in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/212.lean` (with the plane modeled as `ℂ`); this is noted in the module docstring without importing that module, since existing Wikipedia pointer files contain no theorem and the task requires a named `sorry` declaration here.

AMS tags chosen as 11 (Number theory) and 52 (Convex and discrete geometry), matching the tags of `ErdosProblems/212.lean` and the problem's 'number theory' tag; 'arithmetic geometry' concerns only the conditional background results.

erdos_ulam_problem.why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q)` using only Mathlib primitives (`Dense`, `Irrational`, `dist` on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)`) and the repo's scoped `ℝ²` notation; category `research open`, AMS 11 52.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős–Ulam problem

The Erdős–Ulam problem asks whether the Euclidean plane contains a dense set of points
all of whose pairwise Euclidean distances are rational numbers. It was asked by Ulam in 1946.
The expected answer is "no": Tao and Shaffaf showed that a negative answer follows from the
Bombieri–Lang conjecture, and Pasten showed that it also follows from the *abc* conjecture.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Ulam_problem)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)
- J. Solymosi, F. de Zeeuw, *On a question of Erdős and Ulam*,
  [arXiv:0806.3095](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3095)
- J. Shaffaf, *A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming the
  Bombieri–Lang conjecture*, [arXiv:1501.00159](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00159)
-/

namespace ErdosUlamProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
**Erdős–Ulam problem.** Is there a dense set of points in the plane all at rational distances
from one another?

Precisely: does there exist a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is topologically dense in the
whole Euclidean plane and such that for all $p, q \in S$ the Euclidean distance $d(p, q)$ is a
rational number? (For $p = q$ the distance is $0$, which is rational, so the condition only
constrains distinct points.)
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14 51]
theorem erdos_ulam_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q) := by
  sorry

end ErdosUlamProblem
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single yes/no slot is the right decomposition; the conditional results (Bombieri–Lang / abc imply a negative answer), the circle characterization and the Harborth consequence are background and are only mentioned in the module docstring, not stated as theorems.
modeling_decisions: The plane is modeled as `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (repo notation `ℝ²`), not `ℂ` as in the existing ErdosProblems/212.lean; both carry the Euclidean metric and the two statements are equivalent.

'Rational distance' is expressed as `¬ Irrational (dist p q)` (the idiom of Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean) rather than `dist p q ∈ Set.range Rat.cast` (the idiom of ErdosProblems/212.lean); these are definitionally the same condition.
The pairwise condition is quantified over all `p, q ∈ S` including `p = q` (following the decomposition note); since `dist p p = 0` is rational this is equivalent to the `Set.Pairwise` form.
'Dense' is read as topologically dense in all of ℝ²; the empty set is excluded automatically because `Dense ∅` fails in the nonempty space ℝ².

AMS tags chosen as 11 (number theory), 14 (algebraic geometry, for the 'arithmetic geometry' tag) and 51 (geometry). The existing ErdosProblems/212.lean uses 52; a reviewer may prefer adding/substituting 52.

The module docstring cites the Erdős–Ulam Wikipedia page, the Wikipedia unsolved-problems list, erdosproblems.com/212 and the two arXiv papers in the background folder; the file does not import or restate ErdosProblems/212.lean.

/-!
# Erdős–Ulam problem

The Erdős–Ulam problem asks whether the Euclidean plane contains a dense set of points
whose pairwise Euclidean distances are all rational numbers. Ulam asked this in 1946;
Ulam and Erdős conjectured that no such set exists. The problem is open. Assuming the
Bombieri–Lang conjecture (Tao, Shaffaf) or the abc conjecture (Pasten), the answer is
negative.

The same question is stated over `ℂ` as Erdős problem 212 in
`FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/212.lean`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Ulam_problem)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)
- J. Shaffaf, *A solution of the Erdős–Ulam problem on rational distance sets assuming the
  Bombieri–Lang conjecture*, [arXiv:1501.00159](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.00159)
- J. Solymosi, F. de Zeeuw, *On a question of Erdős and Ulam*,
  [arXiv:0806.3095](https://arxiv.org/abs/0806.3095)
-/

namespace ErdosUlamProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
**Erdős–Ulam problem.** Is there a dense set of points in the plane all at rational
distances from one another?

That is, does there exist a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is (topologically) dense in
the whole Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ and such that for all $p, q \in S$ the Euclidean
distance $\lvert p - q \rvert$ is a rational number? (For $p = q$ the distance is $0$, which
is rational, so requiring the condition for all pairs is the same as requiring it for all
pairs of distinct points.)

Ulam and Erdős conjectured that no such set exists. The problem is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem erdos_ulam_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q) := by
  sorry

end ErdosUlamProblem

modeling_decisions: The plane is modeled as `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (repo notation `ℝ²`, as in `Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean`), so `dist` is the Euclidean L² distance; the closely related `ErdosProblems/212.lean` uses `Set ℂ` instead, which is isometric — I chose `ℝ²` to match the Wikipedia-folder idiom and cross-referenced Erdős 212 in the module docstring.
'Rational distance' is expressed as `¬ Irrational (dist p q)`, i.e. `dist p q ∈ Set.range Rat.cast` (same idiom as `RationalDistanceProblem.lean`).

The rationality condition is required for all pairs `p, q ∈ S` including `p = q` (distance 0, rational), which is equivalent to requiring it for distinct pairs (`S.Pairwise`); this follows the decomposition notes.

'Dense' is Mathlib's `Dense S`, i.e. topological density in the whole Euclidean plane, per the article ('dense subset of the Euclidean plane'), not density on a curve; the empty set is not dense in `ℝ²`, so there is no degenerate witness.

Direction of `answer`: `answer(True)` asserts that a dense rational-distance set exists; the conjectured (Ulam/Erdős, conditional on Bombieri–Lang or abc) answer is `False`, but the problem is open so `answer(sorry)` is used.

AMS tags `11 51` (number theory, geometry), matching the tags of the sibling file `RationalDistanceProblem.lean`; the problem's 'arithmetic geometry' tag is covered by 11 (11G) and the planar setting by 51.

modeling_decisions: The 'plane' is modelled as `ℝ²` := `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (the repository's scoped notation), so `dist` is the Euclidean (L2) distance; I checked in a scratch file that `dist p q` rewrites via `EuclideanSpace.dist_eq` to sqrt of the sum of squared coordinate differences. The existing `ErdosProblems/212.lean` formalizes the same question over `ℂ`; I used ℝ² to match the Wikipedia-collection idiom (`RationalDistanceProblem.lean`, `Erdos1082`).

'Dense' is `Dense S`, i.e. topological density in the whole plane (closure S = univ); this excludes the empty set and sets dense only on a line or circle, matching the article's remark that circle examples are 'only dense on their circle, not dense on the whole plane'.

'Rational distance' is expressed as `¬ Irrational (dist p q)`, which is definitionally `dist p q ∈ Set.range ((↑) : ℚ → ℝ)`; this follows the idiom of `Wikipedia/RationalDistanceProblem.lean`. The quantification `∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S` includes p = q, where the distance 0 is rational, so it is equivalent to the `S.Pairwise` formulation.

The question form is rendered as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S, …` per the repo's convention for yes/no questions; `answer(True)` = a dense rational-distance set exists, `answer(False)` = the Ulam/Erdős conjecture. Category `research open` since the problem is open (only conditional results under Bombieri–Lang / abc exist).

AMS tags 11 (number theory) and 51 (geometry), matching the closely related `RationalDistanceProblem.lean`; the conditional results (Bombieri–Lang, abc), the circle characterization and the Harborth consequence are treated as background and not stated, as the decomposition table prescribes.

Module docstring cites the required Wikipedia URL, the list page, erdosproblems.com/212 (with a pointer to the existing `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«212»` formalization, in the style of `Wikipedia/HadwigerNelson.lean`), and the two cited arXiv papers.

erdos_ulam_problem.why: Stated as `answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q)` with ℝ² = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) (repo's scoped notation via `open EuclideanGeometry`). Only existing Mathlib/repo primitives are used (Dense, dist, Irrational, ℝ² notation from FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean).

statement_blocks.erdos_ulam_problem:
/--
**Erdős–Ulam problem.** Is there a dense set of points in the plane all at rational distances
from one another?

That is, does there exist a subset $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ that is (topologically) dense in
the whole Euclidean plane and such that for all $p, q \in S$ the Euclidean distance $|p - q|$
is a rational number?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 51]
theorem erdos_ulam_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧ ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q) := by
  sorry

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős–Ulam problem

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Erdős–Ulam problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erd%C5%91s%E2%80%93Ulam_problem)
-/

namespace ErdosUlamProblem

open EuclideanGeometry

/--
Does the Euclidean plane contain a set that is dense in the whole plane and such that the
Euclidean distance between every two of its points is rational?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 14]
theorem erdos_ulam_problem :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ S : Set ℝ², Dense S ∧
      ∀ p ∈ S, ∀ q ∈ S, ¬ Irrational (dist p q) := by
  sorry

end ErdosUlamProblem
modeling_decisions: Modeled the plane as the repository's `ℝ²`, namely the two-dimensional real Euclidean space, so `dist` is Euclidean distance.
Interpreted “dense” as Mathlib's `Dense S` in the whole ambient Euclidean plane, as clarified by the background article.
Expressed a real distance being rational as `¬ Irrational (dist p q)`, following existing repository usage and Mathlib's definition of `Irrational`; this includes the trivial case `p = q`.
Used `answer(sorry)` for the unanswered yes/no question rather than asserting the conjectured negative answer.
